domain_label: Turlock Independent Personal Care — Business Models & Unit Economics
purpose: A method for reasoning about how each independent personal-care format in Turlock and Stanislaus County is actually run as a business — its service menu and station/chair equipment, its booth-rental versus W-2 labor model, the BarberCosmo / medical-director / Safe-Body-Art licensing gate, the cost structure and labeled benchmark margins, the distributor or medical-procurement supply chain, and the operating decisions that make the format viable or doom it — without ever stating a named business's dollar revenue as fact.
assumptions: no observed per-business financials supplied; every dollar band is a labeled industry-benchmark estimate scaled by an observable size signal (chairs, stations, providers, artists, treatment rooms, format), tagged estimate-not-actual, never a claim of actual revenue for any named business

the universe is the 25 verified independent personal-care businesses in Turlock catalogued in businesses.json (chains, mall/Walmart counters and below-threshold solo/home/booth operators excluded), in a town of ~72,500 with ~8,400 CSU Stanislaus undergraduates and deep Assyrian/Portuguese/Mexican/Punjabi heritage communities

city, county, state and demographic figures used here (population, income, ancestry shares, license requirements, the 2025 manicurist W-2 change) are cited public facts from the deep-dive or labeled derivations, not invented

supplier-to-named-business links are representative inference about the realistic supply universe, not confirmed contracts, except the two self-disclosed cases (Organic Nails SNS dipping; Face&Beyond multi-brand injectables)
cost-structure and margin benchmarks are published industry figures (labor/rent/product-COGS/net) applied as planning priors, not audited operator P&Ls
exclusions: chain and franchise personal-care operations (Great Clips/Sport Clips/Supercuts-type), mall and Walmart nail/beauty counters, and below-threshold solo/home/Instagram-booked operators (the catalog is verified independents only)
stating any actual dollar revenue, profit, or owner income for a specifically named Turlock business as fact
demand-and-saturation market sizing as a standalone deliverable beyond what is needed to judge a format's viability (the per-10k saturation detail lives in the market/reconciled analyses)
non-personal-care retail and product-only e-commerce except where a personal-care format straddles into a retail product-attach arm
tax, legal, employment-classification and medical-licensure advice for an individual operator; this models formats and decisions, not a specific filing or medical-director contract

competency_questions.question: What anchors personal-care demand in Turlock and which heritage/student communities make event-beauty and grooming formats viable that a generic 72k town would not carry?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKET_DEMAND_BASE names the resident/student demand sources with cited figures and HERITAGE_EVENT_DEMAND ties the Assyrian (~25%), Portuguese/Azorean (~7%), Mexican (46% Hispanic) and Punjabi/Sikh communities to the wedding/quinceanera/festival event-beauty capacity each sustains

competency_questions.question: Why does Turlock sustain roughly 25 independents and not far more, and how do Modesto leakage and the demand ceiling cap that count?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DEMAND_CEILING explains the recurring-essential demand cap as the primary governor and MODESTO_LEAKAGE explains the ~15-mile discretionary-spend leakage to the larger regional anchor

competency_questions.question: How are per-format revenue and margin bands estimated honestly when no per-business revenue is public?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BENCHMARK_REVENUE_METHOD states the published-benchmark-times-observable-size-signal method, the estimate-not-actual label, a confidence level and a confirmation path, and COST_STRUCTURE_BENCHMARKS supplies the labor/rent/product-COGS/net backbone it scales

competency_questions.question: What licensing must a barber/cosmetology establishment, a med spa, and a tattoo studio each clear before opening, and which is the binding entry gate?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BARBERCOSMO_LICENSE, MEDSPA_MEDICAL_GATE and BODYART_PERMIT each state the concrete state/county requirement with its public source and identify which is the binding entry gate for that format

competency_questions.question: How does the booth/chair-rental labor model let low-capex formats run, and how did the 2025 manicurist W-2 mandate break it for nail salons?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LABOR_MODEL_LEVER explains how booth/chair rental converts owner revenue to rent and shifts COGS to renters, and WORKER_CLASSIFICATION states the 1/1/2025 manicurist carve-out expiry forcing nail techs to W-2 while hair/skin/barber keep the Borello carve-out

competency_questions.question: What is the distributor-fed input model for the non-medical sub-sector, and how does the CA Vietnamese-American nail wholesale channel differ from the mainstream?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: INPUT_SUPPLY_MODEL describes the low-capex JIT CosmoProf/SalonCentric distributor spine and NAIL_WHOLESALE_CHANNEL names the distinct DTK/ND/Cali/Beauty Zone Vietnamese-American ecosystem, both flagged as representative inference except the self-disclosed links

competency_questions.question: What does it take to run a barber shop or men's grooming format, and how does the Square-booking appointment model and retail product-attach shape it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BARBER_MENS_MODEL describes the per-chair economics, the appointment-app (Get Faded/Godspeed Square) versus walk-in split, the chair-rental owner inversion, and the Noblemens retail grooming-product attach as a higher-margin lever

competency_questions.question: Why is the nail salon the most contested and most margin-pressured format in the set right now, and how does the 2025 W-2 squeeze compound that?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NAIL_SALON_MODEL states the per-station volume model, the locally-crowded read, the weak walk-in-substitutable pricing power, and ties the compounded 2025 margin squeeze to WORKER_CLASSIFICATION

competency_questions.question: Why is med spa the clearest white space yet the hardest to enter, and what is the unit economics behind that?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MEDSPA_MODEL gives the per-provider injectable-led economics, the high gross but capital-and-licensure-gated entry (medical-director + $50k-$150k device capex), and ranks it the top high-barrier white space in SATURATION_WHITESPACE

competency_questions.question: What distinguishes the full-service hair salon and the suite/booth-rental hair model, and where is each one's margin?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: HAIR_SALON_MODEL names the stylist-station economics, the color-bar COGS, the suite/booth-rental inversion (Salon Two Zero Nine) versus full-service house (Bliss/Inspirations), and the per-renter-take versus house-revenue distinction

competency_questions.question: How do the discretionary day-spa and tattoo formats differ in their margin engine and entry barrier?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: DAYSPA_MODEL identifies treatment-room utilization and product-retail attach as the lever for a thin standalone segment, and TATTOO_MODEL pairs its commission/booth-split economics with the low-capex-driven local oversupply and the Safe-Body-Art permit gate

competency_questions.question: Given demand, cost, licensing and saturation, what is the merged go/no-go on adding a given personal-care format in Turlock?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: FORMAT_GO_NOGO composes saturation, cost gate and demand headroom into a defensible add/avoid verdict (no eighth nail salon, sixth barber, sixth tattoo studio; favor med spa, premium destination spa, event/cultural beauty) each conditioned on clearing the licensure and capex gate

glossary.definition: The binding honesty label on every dollar band in this KB: the figure is a published industry benchmark (revenue per chair/station/provider/artist/room) scaled by an observable Turlock size signal, never a reported or claimed actual revenue for any named business.

The dominant labor model in barber and hair: the owner rents a station to an independently-licensed pro who keeps service revenue, issues a 1099 for rent, carries own insurance and books own clients, which converts owner revenue to predictable rent and shifts COGS, scheduling and client risk onto the renter.

CA's temporary AB 5 booth-rental carve-out for manicurists expired Jan 1 2025, so nail techs must now be W-2 employees (hair/skin/barber pros retain the Borello carve-out); it adds ~10-15%+ effective labor cost and is the live 2025 margin shock for the seven nail salons.

The structural requirement that a physician (MD/DO) owns or supervises the medical acts of a med spa while injectors are RNs/NPs/PAs under delegation; combined with $50k-$150k device capex it is the single biggest personal-care entry barrier and the reason only ~3 med spas exist.

The discretionary-spend cap created by Modesto (roughly triple Turlock's population, ~15 miles north) drawing premium med spa, luxury spa days and specialty-tattoo demand north; the single largest unmeasured variable in the sector analysis.

Wedding/quinceanera/festival event-beauty demand from Turlock's deep Assyrian (~25%), Portuguese/Azorean (~7%), near-majority Mexican and Punjabi/Sikh communities — the one structural feature letting a 72k town carry more salon/nail/event capacity than population alone would predict.

An observable proxy (chair count, station count, provider count, artist count, treatment-room count, format) used to scale a published per-unit benchmark into a planning revenue band, in place of unavailable actual sales.

The principle that the 25-business catalog excludes chains, mall/Walmart counters and below-threshold solo/home operators, so every per-10k density figure is a floor and true on-the-ground density is higher; a thin ratio is a counting artifact, not demand headroom.

The sticky, habit-driven, recession-resilient visit rhythm of barber (every 2-4 weeks), nail fills (every 2-3 weeks) and basic cut/color (every 6-10 weeks) on small tickets, the demand floor that anchors the sector count, distinct from discretionary/aspirational med-spa/spa/tattoo cadence.

A distinct CA Vietnamese-American distributor channel (DTK San Jose, ND, Cali/Cal, Beauty Zone Westminster, C8/LA Nail) separate from the CosmoProf/SalonCentric mainstream, enabling fast regional JIT reorder of a broad slow-turn powder/color SKU long-tail plus fast-turn staples.

source_registry.description: heuristic prior estimates for turlock_pc_models work units in absence of supplied datasets
source_registry.citation_or_locator: heuristic prior; no external dataset supplied

nodes.definition: Establish the demand floor every Turlock personal-care format draws on: ~72,500 residents at a median household income of ~$83,000 and a median age of 34.9, plus ~8,400 CSU Stanislaus undergraduates (~9,300 total enrollment) whose term-time presence disproportionately lifts nails, brows/lashes, fades and first tattoos. This base supports a finite number of recurring-cut/fill chairs, and its income — above the county average but below coastal-CA metros — favors volume value formats (value nail/barber) over premium-only ones, which is exactly the observed mix. All figures are cited public facts; this is the size of the pie before any format question is asked.

included: resident population, income, median age
CSU Stanislaus student demand
the volume-vs-premium format tilt income implies

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a population, income, age, or enrollment figure is updated

pros.claim: Sizing the base from cited public figures grounds every format judgment in real local demand instead of national job-board noise
pros.example: the ~72,500 residents at ~$83k median income set a defensible volume-format tilt no premium-only concept can ignore

cons.claim: A population average invites the error of treating term-time student demand as year-round capacity
cons.example: over-building lash/nail chairs for a 12-month calendar when CSU demand swings with the academic term

failure_modes: treating the resident base as the independents' addressable revenue without subtracting chain and gray-market capture
ignoring the term-time swing of student demand and over-building for a flat calendar
acceptance_tests: the demand base cites population, income, median age and student enrollment with sources, and states the volume-vs-premium tilt the income level implies
revisit_triggers: a Census ACS refresh changes population or income
CSU Stanislaus enrollment shifts materially
the income level moves enough to change the volume-vs-premium tilt

nodes.definition: Tie Turlock's unusual heritage depth to the event-beauty capacity it sustains. The town holds California's 4th-highest Assyrian-ancestry share (~a quarter of the city), a ~7% Portuguese/Azorean ancestry, a near-majority Mexican base (46% Hispanic) and a Punjabi/Sikh community. Each generates wedding / quinceanera / festival event-driven beauty demand — formal updos, bridal teams, brow/lash, henna-adjacent services, group bookings — that a generic 72k town would not carry. This is the lone structural expander pushing the count modestly above population alone, a defensible under-formalized niche national chains structurally cannot serve.

included: Assyrian, Portuguese/Azorean, Mexican, Punjabi/Sikh shares with sources
the event-beauty demand each community generates
why the niche is chain-resistant
excluded: the cost structure of each format

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a heritage community's size or the event demand it generates changes

pros.claim: Mapping heritage communities to event-beauty demand explains why the count runs above what a generic 72k town would carry
pros.example: Assyrian/Mexican/Punjabi wedding-and-quinceanera demand sustaining bridal/updo/lash capacity across salons and nail shops

cons.claim: Event demand is culturally durable but episodic, so it can be mistaken for steady year-round capacity
cons.example: staffing for peak wedding-season group bookings that idle between events

failure_modes: assuming a large community implies unlimited steady format headroom
treating episodic event demand as a flat annual revenue line
acceptance_tests: each heritage community is given its cited share and the specific event-beauty demand it generates, distinguishing episodic from steady demand
revisit_triggers: ancestry shares shift in a Census refresh
a heritage community grows or contracts via migration
a new event-beauty format tied to an under-served community opens

nodes.definition: Account for the discretionary-spend cap: Modesto, roughly triple the population and ~15 miles north, is the regional retail/medical gravity center. Higher-ticket and specialty demand — premium med spa, plastics-adjacent aesthetics, luxury spa days, specialty tattoo artists — leaks north, so Turlock keeps the recurring-essential convenience spend and loses the make-a-day-of-it discretionary spend. The direction is certain (Modesto is far larger and close) but the dollar magnitude is the single largest unmeasured variable in the sector; any format judgment that ignores this leakage will over-state Turlock headroom for discretionary cross-shopped formats while leaving neighborhood-loyal recurring formats largely unaffected.

included: Modesto's size and proximity
which spend categories leak north
which formats are most vs least exposed
excluded: a measured leakage figure (the magnitude is unknown)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: regional personal-care supply in Modesto or Turlock shifts

pros.claim: Naming the leakage explains why population alone over-predicts Turlock's premium personal-care count
pros.example: premium aesthetics leaking to Modesto, so a high-end med spa must out-compete on convenience and trust, not just open

cons.claim: The leakage magnitude is unknown, so it can be over- or under-applied to a given format
cons.example: assuming all discretionary spend leaks when downtown Turlock retains loyal tattoo and spa clients

failure_modes: applying the cap uniformly to neighborhood-loyal recurring formats that do not cross-shop
treating the unmeasured magnitude as if it were a measured count
acceptance_tests: the analysis states Modesto's size and distance, ranks formats by leakage exposure, and flags the magnitude as unknown
revisit_triggers: a major personal-care development opens in Modesto or Turlock
a cross-shop leakage study is produced
Turlock premium-format density changes

nodes.definition: Establish the primary cap on the sector count: it is demand-governed, not supply-governed. A fixed pool of ~72,500 residents at ~$83k income supports a finite number of recurring-cut/fill chairs, and that demand ceiling — not supply-chain friction — sets the ~25 equilibrium. Personal Care splits into recurring-essential cadence (barber every 2-4 weeks, nail fills every 2-3 weeks, cut/color every 6-10 weeks; sticky and recession-resilient) and discretionary/aspirational cadence (med-spa injectables, spa days, lash, tattoos; income-elastic, first cut when budgets tighten). Nail and barber sit at or near local saturation, so an eighth nail salon mostly reshuffles share rather than growing the pie; the count is anchored by the recurring-essential floor.

included: the demand-governed-not-supply-governed cap
recurring-essential vs discretionary cadence split
the at-saturation read for nail and barber

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a demand-pool, cadence, or saturation figure changes

pros.claim: Framing the count as demand-governed corrects the error of reading supply-chain ease as room to add chairs
pros.example: an eighth nail salon reshuffling share in a fixed recurring-fill pool rather than growing demand

cons.claim: The cadence split is an industry-pattern observation, not a measured local visit log, so the ceiling is a reasoned estimate
cons.example: treating the recurring-essential floor as a precise chair count rather than a band

failure_modes: reading low supply-chain friction as demand headroom for at-saturation formats
conflating sticky recurring demand with elastic discretionary demand in one ceiling
acceptance_tests: the analysis states the demand-governed cap, separates recurring-essential from discretionary cadence, and names nail and barber as at-or-near local saturation
revisit_triggers: population or income shifts the recurring-fill pool
a visit-cadence or spend study lands
a format's local count crosses its saturation read

nodes.definition: Lay down the published, cited cost-structure backbone every format model is read against: hair-salon labor (wages + 30-40% commission + payroll) ~40-55% of revenue (largest line), rent/occupancy ~6-12%, product COGS ~5-12%, net ~8-15% typical (20%+ top performers, US avg ~8%); barber lower COGS than hair; nail historically thin on low tickets; med spa higher gross on injectables but gated by device lease/depreciation ($1.5k-$4k/mo/device), medical-director/injector labor and malpractice insurance; tattoo and day spa rent/split- and utilization-driven. These are PBA/Vagaro/joinblvd planning benchmarks, not audited operator P&Ls, and they are the lens that turns a revenue band into a margin reality — booth-rental inverts the labor/COGS lines onto renters.

included: labor/rent/product-COGS/net benchmark ranges by sub-category
the med-spa capital-intensity caveat
the planning-prior status and booth-rental inversion

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a published cost-structure benchmark or device-lease rate is revised

pros.claim: Pairing every revenue band with the labor and net benchmark stops high gross from being mistaken for high profit
pros.example: a med spa benchmarking high injectable gross still gated by device lease and malpractice cost, which the backbone makes explicit

cons.claim: Published benchmarks lag and average away the booth-rental inversion and local pricing that move real Turlock margins
cons.example: the 40-55% labor benchmark overstates owner cost for a chair-rental barber shop collecting rent

failure_modes: importing a national benchmark without adjusting for booth-rental inversion or local value pricing
reading a benchmark range as a single point estimate
acceptance_tests: labor, rent, product-COGS and net benchmark ranges are stated by sub-category with sources and labeled planning priors, with the med-spa capital caveat and the booth-rental inversion noted
revisit_triggers: a new industry benchmark guide is published
minimum wage or product-cost inflation shifts the labor or COGS share
the med-spa device-lease cost moves

nodes.definition: Define the only honest way to attach a revenue band to a format when no per-business revenue is public: take a published industry benchmark (barber $60k-$100k rev/chair; hair ~$245k avg salon / ~$76k rev/employee; nail $250k-$460k/location, ~$34 rev/capita national; med spa $300k-$600k rev/provider with ~$1.4M avg single-location AmSpa national; tattoo 1-2 artist $60k-$150k, 3-5 artist $150k-$350k) and scale it by an observable Turlock size signal (chairs, stations, providers, artists, rooms), haircut for a sub-metro value market, then tag the result estimate-not-actual, assign a confidence and name the confirmation path. Two national-benchmark-as-estimate flags travel always: the med-spa ~$1.4M/location and nail ~$34/capita are national AmSpa/Statista benchmarks, NEVER Turlock facts, and no figure attributes revenue to a named business.

included: benchmark-times-size-signal method
the estimate-not-actual label, confidence and confirmation path
the national-benchmark-as-estimate flags for med spa and nail
excluded: stating a named business's actual revenue

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a benchmark, a size signal, or the availability of confirming data changes

pros.claim: A labeled benchmark band gives a defensible planning number without ever claiming a private business's actual revenue
pros.example: a 4-chair barber at $60k-$100k/chair scaling to a band tagged estimate with a sub-metro haircut and a confidence level

cons.claim: A benchmark band can be over-trusted if the size signal is mis-observed or the national flag is dropped
cons.example: quoting the ~$1.4M med-spa average as a Turlock figure instead of a national AmSpa benchmark

failure_modes: dropping the estimate-not-actual label and presenting a band as a fact
citing the med-spa $1.4M or nail $34/capita national benchmark as a local actual
acceptance_tests: every revenue band produced carries the estimate-not-actual label, a confidence level, the size signal used, and the two national-benchmark flags are stated where med-spa or nail figures appear
revisit_triggers: a published per-chair/per-station/per-provider/per-artist benchmark is updated
a format's observable size signal changes
a local confirmation source (sales-tax data) becomes available

nodes.definition: Explain the sector's defining labor variable: booth/chair rental dominates barber and hair. Owners rent stations to independently-licensed pros who keep service revenue, issue a 1099 for rent, carry own insurance and book own clients — Salon Two Zero Nine explicitly advertises independent stylists and private suites, a named suite-rental model. This converts the owner's revenue to predictable rent rather than service margin and shifts COGS, scheduling and client risk onto the renter, so owner-level and operator-level economics diverge and must never be summed. Owner-operator or small W-2 crews dominate single-chair shops and walk-in tattoo studios; med spa is the structural exception requiring medical-director oversight.

included: how booth/chair rental inverts owner economics to rent
which formats use it (barber, hair) vs owner-operator/W-2 (single-chair, tattoo)
the owner-vs-renter divergence
excluded: the manicurist W-2 mandate (its own node)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a booth-rental rate, a format conversion, or a classification ruling occurs

pros.claim: Naming booth rental as the owner-revenue inversion shows why house revenue and per-renter take are two different things
pros.example: a suite-rental salon collecting rent while each stylist carries own COGS and client book

cons.claim: Rental terms vary, so the inversion is a structural fact whose magnitude depends on the specific rent deal
cons.example: a chair at $150/week versus $350/week producing very different owner economics

failure_modes: summing house rent revenue and per-renter service take as if one operator earned both
modeling a chair-rental owner at full service-labor benchmark and missing the rent inversion
acceptance_tests: the analysis states how booth/chair rental converts owner revenue to rent, names the barber/hair formats that use it, and flags the owner-vs-renter divergence
revisit_triggers: per-chair rent benchmarks shift
an owner converts between full-service and chair-rental
a classification ruling alters the booth-rental carve-out

nodes.definition: Map the realistic supply universe of the non-medical sub-sector, flagged as representative inference except self-disclosed links: a low-capex, distributor-fed, consumables-light, just-in-time input model. Barber/men's grooming draws CosmoProf, SalonCentric, BuyBarber, Vip Barber (Wahl/Andis/Oster) for blades, oil, Barbicide and retail pomade; hair salons draw SalonCentric/CosmoProf (Redken/Wella/Olaplex) for color, developer and extensions; spa draws SalonCentric/CosmoProf and skincare-specialty for wax, skincare and massage oils; tattoo draws tattoo-specialty distributors for mandated pre-sterile single-use cartridges and commercial inks only. National distributors with CA warehouses plus pro e-commerce deliver in 1-5 days, so input friction shapes mix and margin but not the count.

included: broadline barber/hair/spa distributors and tattoo-specialty supply per format
the low-capex JIT 1-5 day delivery model
the inference label on supplier-to-business links
excluded: the distinct Vietnamese-American nail channel (its own node)
the med-spa medical procurement (covered in the med-spa gate)

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a supplier relationship or a tattoo supply regulation changes

pros.claim: A format-to-supplier map shows the realistic, verified-to-serve-this-geography supply universe behind each non-medical model
pros.example: barbers drawing Wahl/Andis clippers and retail pomade from CosmoProf/BuyBarber on a 1-5 day JIT cycle

cons.claim: Supplier-to-named-business links are inference and can be mistaken for confirmed contracts
cons.example: asserting a specific barber shop buys from a named distributor without a cited source

failure_modes: upgrading a representative supplier link to a stated fact
ignoring the tattoo regulatory constraint (single-use, commercial inks only) that shapes its supply
acceptance_tests: each non-medical format has its key supplier nodes named with the inference label, and the tattoo single-use/commercial-ink constraint is stated
revisit_triggers: a named distributor enters or exits the Valley
a documented supplier contract surfaces

nodes.definition: Establish the baseline licensing every barber, hair, nail and esthetics establishment must clear: the CA Board of Barbering & Cosmetology (BarberCosmo) requires individual licenses (displayed) and an establishment license, plus sanitation/plumbing minimums (toilets, hot/cold running water, handwashing) before opening, with booth renters each licensed and the establishment verifying currency. This is a real but routine gate that does not by itself cap the count — it is the non-negotiable floor under barber, men's grooming, hair, nail and esthetics formats, cheaper and faster than the med-spa medical or body-art gates, and it is where the establishment's currency-of-license obligation for booth renters is enforced.

included: individual + establishment BarberCosmo licenses and sanitation minimums
the establishment's booth-renter currency obligation
the routine-floor status for non-medical formats

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a BarberCosmo establishment requirement or sanitation standard changes

pros.claim: Treating the BarberCosmo establishment license as the routine floor prevents a model that ignores the sanitation plan-check gate
pros.example: a hair salon budgeting establishment licensure and plumbing minimums before lease signing

cons.claim: The BarberCosmo floor is routine, so it can lull an operator into underestimating the costlier med-spa and body-art gates
cons.example: assuming a modest establishment license means easy entry into any personal-care format

failure_modes: skipping the sanitation/plumbing check and discovering a non-conforming space after build-out
confusing the routine BarberCosmo floor with the costlier medical or body-art gates
acceptance_tests: the individual + establishment BarberCosmo licenses, the sanitation minimums and the booth-renter currency obligation are stated with the public source as the routine non-medical floor
revisit_triggers: BarberCosmo establishment requirements or fees change
a sanitation/plumbing standard is revised
a format changes services enough to require re-licensing

nodes.definition: Define the live 2025 worker-classification shock: hair/skin/barber pros retain the Borello booth-rental carve-out (separate business, own insurance, written agreement, 1099), but CA's temporary AB 5 carve-out for manicurists expired Jan 1 2025, so nail techs must now be W-2 employees. This adds ~10-15%+ to effective labor cost (payroll tax + workers' comp + admin + PAGA-misclassification exposure) and disproportionately affects the Vietnamese-immigrant labor base. Stacked on already-weak, walk-in-substitutable nail pricing power, it produces compounded margin compression — the single biggest operating-model disruptor in the sector right now and a force that hits only the seven nail salons.

included: the Borello carve-out retained by hair/skin/barber
the 1/1/2025 manicurist W-2 mandate and its ~10-15%+ cost step-up
the compounded nail margin squeeze
excluded: the booth-rental model generally (its own node)
the nail unit economics band itself

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a worker-classification ruling or the nail labor step-up estimate changes

pros.claim: Stating the W-2 mandate as a 2025 cost step-up corrects the assumption that nail labor still runs on the cheaper rental model
pros.example: a nail salon absorbing payroll tax and workers' comp it did not carry under the prior booth-rental arrangement

cons.claim: The ~10-15%+ step-up is an industry estimate and per-business absorption (price hike, hour cut, owner absorption) is unobservable

nodes.definition: Establish the binding entry gate for the med-spa tier: a physician (MD/DO) medical-director oversight structure plus a corporate-practice-of-medicine arrangement, injectables procured as FDA-regulated prescription products through authorized medical distributors (McKesson, Pipeline Medical; Allergan/Galderma/Evolus/Revance/Merz brands), cold-chain lot-tracked short-dated FIFO inventory, and $50k-$150k device capex (or $1.5k-$4k/mo/device leasing). Med-spa white space must be read as high-barrier-under-built, not easy-to-enter; Face&Beyond's self-disclosed multi-brand injectables are the documented input link.

nodes.definition: Establish the licensing gate for the tattoo/piercing format: CA's Safe Body Art Act plus Stanislaus County Environmental Health require a Body Art Facility health permit, registered practitioners, pre-sterilized single-use needles/cartridges, commercially manufactured inks only, a steam autoclave for any reusable instruments, an infection-control plan, plan-check and self-inspection. It is a real regulatory gate but a low-capex one (~$2,000-$6,000/station plus a shared autoclave), which is exactly why tattoo runs at ~2x national per-capita density in Turlock — the low capital cost enables the observed oversupply, with the five studios (Colossal, Main Street, Moezart, Rebelucio, Third Eye) competing on artist reputation rather than entry difficulty.

nodes.definition: Synthesize the per-format saturation read that explains why ~25 is the equilibrium and where headroom remains, all as a coverage floor (independents-only, chains/counters/solo excluded, so thin ratios are counting artifacts not headroom). nodes.definition: Compose the merged go/no-go verdict on adding or running a given personal-care format, the synthesis the whole KB builds toward. It intersects three lenses: demand headroom (SATURATION_WHITESPACE), the cost/licensure gate (BARBERCOSMO_LICENSE, MEDSPA_MEDICAL_GATE, BODYART_PERMIT, WORKER_CLASSIFICATION, CAPEX_SPECTRUM), and the margin reality (COST_STRUCTURE_BENCHMARKS, LABOR_MODEL_LEVER). The reconciled rule: do not add an eighth nail salon, a sixth barber, or a sixth tattoo studio (at or above local saturation); the defensible headroom is med spa (only if you can clear the physician-oversight + six-figure-capex wall and out-compete Modesto on convenience/trust), premium destination spa (recapture the day-spa spend leaking north), and event/cultural beauty (a format no chain can serve). A white space that is demand-true but capital-and-licensure-gated is a no-go until the gate is cleared — the binding constraint at the top tier is the entry wall, not the input cost.

conflict_axes.name: coverage_floor_vs_lived_saturation
conflict_axes.description: A thin independents-only per-10k ratio (nail 0.97 vs ~3.4 national) conflicts with the lived-crowded competitive read once chains, counters and solo operators are remembered.
poles: read the thin ratio as headroom
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat the catalog as a coverage floor: a thin ratio is a counting artifact, and nail/barber/tattoo are crowded in lived terms

conflict_axes.name: heritage_event_demand_vs_modesto_cap
conflict_axes.description: Heritage event demand raises the viable format count while Modesto's draw caps discretionary spend; a format read can over-weight either force.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: apply heritage event demand to chain-resistant cultural-beauty formats and the Modesto cap to discretionary cross-shopped ones

conflict_axes.name: demand_headroom_vs_cost_gate
conflict_axes.description: A format with real demand headroom may still be capital-and-licensure-gated (med spa) so demand-true is not the same as enterable.
poles: enter only where the cost gate clears
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: treat a demand-true but capital/licensure-gated white space as a no-go until the binding gate is cleared

conflict_axes.name: high_gross_vs_thin_net
conflict_axes.description: High-gross formats (med spa injectables) can post strong revenue while netting thin after device lease, malpractice and director labor, so revenue must never be read as profit.
poles: respect the thin net after capital
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always pair the revenue band with its capital-intensity and net benchmark before judging attractiveness

conflict_axes.name: booth_rent_owner_vs_renter_economics
conflict_axes.description: Booth/chair rental lets the owner collect predictable rent but pushes COGS and client risk onto renters, so house revenue and per-renter take are two different things.
poles: read house revenue as owner earnings
separate owner rent from renter service take
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: never sum the house rent band and the per-renter service take; model them as distinct operator and renter lines

conflict_axes.name: cultural_durability_vs_margin_pressure
conflict_axes.description: A culturally durable recurring format (nail) can be the most margin-pressured, so deep demand does not imply a safe margin.
poles: treat recurring demand as a growth lane
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: defend the existing recurring count but do not add to a margin-compressed, locally-crowded format on demand depth alone

conflict_axes.name: medspa_capex_vs_leasing
conflict_axes.description: Owning $50k-$150k aesthetic devices burdens entry cash while leasing at $1.5k-$4k/mo eases entry but adds a recurring fixed cost; the entry-cash versus ongoing-cost trade.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: lease where utilization is uncertain or entry cash is tight, buy where provider volume services the depreciation

conflict_axes.name: national_benchmark_vs_local_actual
conflict_axes.description: National benchmarks (med-spa ~$1.4M/location, nail ~$34/capita) can drift toward being stated as Turlock facts, conflicting with the honesty rule that no figure is a local actual.
poles: quote the national benchmark as the figure
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: always tag the med-spa $1.4M and nail $34/capita as national benchmarks and never as a Turlock or named-business actual

conflict_axes.name: low_capex_oversupply_vs_high_capex_suppression
conflict_axes.description: Low per-station capex (tattoo) enables oversupply while high capex plus licensure (med spa) suppresses entry into white space; the same capex spectrum cuts both ways.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: avoid the low-capex oversupplied formats and target the high-capex suppressed white space only with the capital to clear it

edge_cases.description: The 2025 manicurist W-2 mandate lands on top of already-weak nail pricing power
edge_cases.trigger: the AB 5 carve-out expiry forces W-2 payroll onto a price-posted nail salon
edge_cases.mitigation: model the ~10-15%+ labor step-up against weak walk-in pricing power and treat the nail margin as compounded-compressed

edge_cases.description: A med-spa concept is planned without securing the physician medical-director structure
edge_cases.trigger: an aesthetics operator budgets devices but not the corporate-practice-of-medicine oversight
edge_cases.mitigation: confirm the medical-director and corporate-practice structure before scoping the med spa; it is the binding gate

edge_cases.description: Med-spa device capex is budgeted as a one-time buy when leasing is the cash-flow workaround
edge_cases.trigger: a six-figure $50k-$150k device purchase strains entry cash
edge_cases.mitigation: model the $1.5k-$4k/mo lease workaround against utilization before committing entry cash to a device purchase

edge_cases.description: A booth-rental hair house revenue and the per-renter take are summed as one operator's income
edge_cases.trigger: a suite-rental salon's collected rent is added to each stylist's service take
edge_cases.mitigation: keep the house rent band and the per-renter service take as distinct lines that are never summed

edge_cases.description: A cold-chain failure spoils lot-tracked short-dated injectables at a med spa
edge_cases.trigger: a refrigeration lapse on FDA-regulated FIFO injectable inventory
edge_cases.mitigation: monitor cold-chain integrity continuously and model spoilage and short-date loss into the injectable cost

edge_cases.description: A thin independents-only nail per-10k ratio is read as room to add a salon
edge_cases.trigger: someone cites nail 0.97 vs ~3.4 national as headroom
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the catalog as a coverage floor: the thin ratio is a counting artifact and nail is locally crowded

edge_cases.description: The med-spa ~$1.4M or nail ~$34/capita national benchmark is reported as a Turlock figure
edge_cases.trigger: a national AmSpa or Statista benchmark is quoted as a local actual
edge_cases.mitigation: flag both as national-not-Turlock benchmarks and lead with the haircut Turlock band

edge_cases.description: A named business's revenue is requested or asserted as an actual figure
edge_cases.trigger: a question demands the real sales of a specific Turlock salon or studio
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse to state actual revenue; provide only a labeled benchmark estimate with confidence and the size signal used

edge_cases.description: A supplier-to-named-business link is upgraded from inference to a stated contract
edge_cases.trigger: an answer asserts a specific salon buys from a named distributor without a source
edge_cases.mitigation: keep supplier links labeled representative inference except the documented Organic Nails (SNS) and Face&Beyond (injectables) cases

edge_cases.description: A demand-true white space is treated as enterable while a capital/licensure gate blocks it
edge_cases.trigger: a med-spa or premium-spa headroom call ignores the medical-director or device-capex gate
edge_cases.mitigation: run every white space through the capital/licensure gate before issuing a go verdict

edge_cases.description: Cash-intensive nail or tattoo throughput makes the revenue band understate true volume
edge_cases.trigger: a cash-heavy format's reported revenue is treated as its full throughput
edge_cases.mitigation: treat the cash-heavy bands as conservative and flag the unmeasured cash-gap rather than over-trusting the figure

workflow.action: Size the resident and student demand floor
workflow.description: State the population, income, median age and student enrollment as cited facts and the volume-vs-premium tilt
workflow.gate: population, income, age and enrollment are stated with sources and the volume-vs-premium tilt is named

workflow.action: Map heritage communities to event-beauty demand
workflow.description: Tie each ancestry share to the wedding/quinceanera/festival demand it generates
workflow.gate: all four communities have cited shares and named event-beauty demand

workflow.description: Identify which discretionary spend leaks north and which formats are exposed
workflow.gate: Modesto size/distance stated, formats ranked by exposure, magnitude flagged unknown

workflow.description: State the demand-governed cap, the recurring-vs-discretionary cadence split and the at-saturation read
workflow.gate: the demand-governed cap and cadence split are stated and nail/barber are named at saturation

workflow.description: State labor/rent/COGS/net benchmarks by sub-category with sources and the booth-rental inversion
workflow.gate: labor, rent, COGS and net ranges are stated as cited planning priors with the med-spa capital caveat

workflow.description: Define benchmark-times-size-signal banding with the estimate label and the national-benchmark flags
workflow.gate: every band carries the estimate-not-actual label, a confidence, a size signal and the national flags where they apply

workflow.action: Map the labor and supply levers
workflow.description: Explain the booth/chair-rental inversion and the distributor and nail-channel supply model
workflow.gate: the booth-rental owner inversion and the distributor/nail-channel nodes are stated with the inference label

workflow.action: Establish the licensing and capex gates
workflow.description: State the BarberCosmo floor, the W-2 mandate, the med-spa medical gate, the body-art permit and the capex spectrum
workflow.gate: the routine BarberCosmo floor, the 2025 W-2 mandate, the medical/body-art gates and the capex spectrum are stated with sources

workflow.action: Model each recurring-essential format's unit economics
workflow.description: For barber/men's, hair and nail, state the size signal, cost center, labeled band and saturation tie
workflow.gate: each recurring format names its cost center, labeled band and the gate or lever that decides viability

workflow.action: Model the discretionary and high-barrier formats
workflow.description: Tie med-spa to the medical/capex gate and high-gross-thin-net, and day-spa/tattoo to leakage and oversupply
workflow.gate: the med-spa capital/licensure gate, the high-gross-thin-net caveat and the day-spa/tattoo leakage and oversupply reads are stated

workflow.action: Synthesize the per-format saturation and white space
workflow.description: Give the at-saturation/white-space read on a coverage-floor basis and rank the white space
workflow.gate: each format has a saturation read and the white space is ranked behind the four forces

priority_rationale: The demand floor, heritage event demand, Modesto leakage and the demand ceiling come first because every format judgment depends on knowing the size and shape of demand and the demand-governed cap on the count; the cost-structure backbone, labeled-revenue method, booth-rental labor lever and distributor/nail-channel supply map next, because they are the lenses that turn demand into unit economics; the BarberCosmo, 2025 W-2, med-spa medical, body-art and capex gates next, because they decide enterability independent of demand and the top-tier entry wall; the seven format models then apply all of that to concrete named businesses; and the saturation synthesis and merged go/no-go come last because they compose every upstream output into a defensible add/avoid verdict on a coverage-floor basis.

dominance_rules.rule: The honesty label dominates any revenue claim
dominance_rules.rationale: no per-business revenue is public, so a band may never be presented as an actual figure
dominance_rules.trigger: any dollar figure is attached to a named business or format
dominance_rules.action: tag it estimate-not-actual with a confidence and size signal, and refuse an actual-revenue claim

dominance_rules.rule: The capital/licensure gate dominates demand headroom in any entry verdict
dominance_rules.rationale: a demand-true white space that cannot clear the medical-director, body-art or capex gate is not enterable
dominance_rules.trigger: a go recommendation rests on demand alone
dominance_rules.action: withhold the go until the binding capital/licensure gate is shown clearable

dominance_rules.rule: Net after capital dominates gross revenue in judging attractiveness
dominance_rules.rationale: high-gross med-spa formats still net thin after device lease, malpractice and director labor
dominance_rules.trigger: a format is judged by its revenue band alone
dominance_rules.action: pair the band with its capital-intensity and net benchmark before deciding

dominance_rules.rule: The coverage-floor rule dominates a thin per-10k ratio
dominance_rules.rationale: the catalog excludes chains, counters and solo operators, so a thin ratio is a counting artifact not headroom
dominance_rules.trigger: a thin independents-only density is cited as room to grow
dominance_rules.action: read the ratio as a floor and apply the lived-crowded saturation instead

dominance_rules.rule: The national-benchmark flag dominates the med-spa and nail figures
dominance_rules.rationale: the ~$1.4M/location and ~$34/capita figures are national benchmarks, never Turlock or named-business actuals
dominance_rules.trigger: a national benchmark is quoted toward a local figure
dominance_rules.action: flag it national-not-Turlock and lead with the haircut local band

dominance_rules.rule: Saturation dominates demand depth for at-saturation formats
dominance_rules.rationale: a deep recurring base does not justify adding to a locally-crowded, margin-pressured format
dominance_rules.trigger: an addition is proposed for nail, barber or tattoo
dominance_rules.action: default to no-add and defend the existing count

dominance_rules.rule: The owner-renter split dominates a summed booth-rental figure
dominance_rules.rationale: house rent and per-renter service take are two different things and must not be summed
dominance_rules.trigger: a booth-rental house revenue and per-renter take are combined
dominance_rules.action: report them as distinct operator and renter lines

dominance_rules.rule: Documented links dominate inferred supplier links
dominance_rules.rationale: only Organic Nails (SNS) and Face&Beyond (injectables) have self-disclosed input links; the rest are inference
dominance_rules.action: label it inference unless it is one of the two documented cases

anti_rework_rules.rule: Attach the estimate-not-actual label when the band is first produced, not after review
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a revenue figure circulating as a fact and having to be retracted

anti_rework_rules.rule: Confirm the medical-director and corporate-practice structure before scoping a med spa
anti_rework_rules.prevents: redesigning an aesthetics concept after the physician-oversight gate proves unmet

anti_rework_rules.rule: Flag the med-spa $1.4M and nail $34/capita as national benchmarks from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a national benchmark hardening into a stated Turlock figure that must later be corrected

anti_rework_rules.rule: Pair every revenue band with its net-after-capital benchmark in the same step
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a high-gross med-spa format being approved before the thin net is seen

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run a white space through the capital/licensure gate before calling it an opportunity
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recommending a demand-true but capital-gated format and reversing the call

anti_rework_rules.rule: Model the nail margin with the 2025 W-2 step-up, not the expired booth-rental carve-out
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a nail plan failing on a labor-cost shock the old rental model hid

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep the booth-rental house revenue and per-renter take as separate lines from the outset
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an inflated owner-income figure that double-counts renter service revenue

anti_rework_rules.rule: Keep supplier-to-business links labeled inference except the two documented cases
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an inferred supply link hardening into an asserted contract that must later be corrected

iteration_protocol.trigger: CDTFA or Turlock Finance personal-care sales-tax data becomes available
iteration_protocol.action: replace the labeled revenue bands with confirmed figures and re-rank confidence

iteration_protocol.trigger: a Census ACS refresh changes population, income or ancestry shares
iteration_protocol.action: re-size the demand floor and re-map the heritage event demand and saturation reads

iteration_protocol.trigger: a further worker-classification ruling or a re-estimate of the nail W-2 step-up lands
iteration_protocol.action: update the nail labor cost and the compounded-squeeze read

iteration_protocol.trigger: med-spa device capex, injectable cost or a medical-director rule changes
iteration_protocol.action: re-evaluate the med-spa entry gate and the high-barrier white-space verdict

iteration_protocol.trigger: a format opens or closes, changing a per-format count
iteration_protocol.action: update the saturation read and the merged go/no-go for that format

iteration_protocol.trigger: a cross-shop Modesto-leakage study or a gray-market solo-operator count is produced
iteration_protocol.action: replace the behavioral leakage estimate and the coverage-floor assumption and re-rank the white space

iteration_protocol.trigger: a BarberCosmo or Safe-Body-Art requirement or a distributor/nail-channel relationship changes
iteration_protocol.action: update the licensing-gate and supply nodes and any format whose entry the change affects
